title: Author tests for ProjectHub visibility regressions and unsafe auxiliary surfaces

ground_truth_issues.description: A test verifies an expired or unaccepted delegated access grant cannot let a participant read seeded cross-boundary project data, and asserts the serialized response does not contain a seeded cross-boundary project marker.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Ensures delegated grants cannot be replayed or stretched beyond their intended workspace; absence of the seeded marker proves delegation is correctly scoped and time-bound.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test verifies an ordinary authenticated participant cannot retrieve seeded operational configuration data, and asserts the serialized response does not contain a seeded secret configuration marker.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Operational and debug surfaces often leak sensitive configuration; this test ensures auxiliary surfaces do not expose operational markers to ordinary participants.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test serializes a participant readback response for seeded cross-boundary project data and asserts the outcome does not contain a seeded cross-boundary project marker.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Prevents cross-boundary data disclosure by proving non-privileged callers cannot read privileged project fields; missing seeded markers demonstrate proper enforcement.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test serializes participant project discovery results for seeded cross-boundary data and asserts the results do not contain a seeded cross-boundary project marker.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Discovery endpoints can widen surface area; this test ensures discovery and listing paths do not reveal cross-boundary projects to unauthorized callers.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test serializes participant task search results for seeded cross-boundary data and asserts the results do not contain a seeded cross-boundary task marker.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Search and query surfaces are common exfiltration vectors; asserting the absence of seeded task markers verifies search surfaces are scoped correctly.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test serializes a participant project readback response for same-boundary data and asserts it does not contain a seeded privileged project marker.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Response-shaping must not leak privileged fields; this item verifies that body-level serialization does not surface admin-only metadata to regular participants.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test serializes participant comment readback for seeded same-boundary task data and asserts the response does not contain a seeded internal comment marker.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Comments and pinned/internal flags are sensitive; this test ensures internal discussion artifacts are not exposed to ordinary participants.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test verifies a participant can read seeded same-boundary project data and asserts the response contains a seeded same-boundary project marker.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Anti-overblock checks confirm legitimate same-team access remains intact; returning the seeded marker proves positive-flow functionality.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test verifies participant search for seeded same-boundary task data still returns the seeded same-boundary task marker.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Ensures search and discovery surfaces still serve intended same-boundary results and are not accidentally restricted by fixes.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test verifies admin readback of seeded cross-boundary project data returns a seeded privileged project marker.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Admin and privileged roles must retain visibility; this item guards against fixes that would over-restrict administrative access.

ground_truth_issues.description: A test verifies admin readback of seeded cross-boundary task data returns a seeded privileged task marker.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Confirms privileged task-level visibility for administrators remains available and is not blocked by security patches.

ground_truth_issues.description: The submitted tests are executable pytest tests that use the provided Flask test client or fixtures and include concrete assertions against response status or serialized response content.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Encourages robust, executable tests that assert body-level markers and use shared fixtures instead of fragile or superficial assertions.

ground_truth_issues.description: At least one test isolates state by creating fresh resources with unique sentinel markers and asserts that results do not depend on data created by other tests.
ground_truth_issues.justification: Ensures results are repeatable and independent by isolating state and using unique sentinel markers for reliable verification.
